Use case: sketch-to-render. Create a photorealistic square architectural image correcting a misleading parking court.
Image 1 is the EXACT geometry reference and camera for the replacement front view. Image 2 supplies ONLY cream stucco, bronze frames, timber entry, terracotta flower-pattern screen, warm Mexican tropical character and lighting. Do NOT copy Image 2's tiny short hatchback or spacious-looking driveway.
Use Image 1's oblique street-left camera so that the full LENGTH of the parked car and both end gaps are apparent. Keep straight verticals. Car is a real, unbranded medium sedan 4.50 m long and 1.85 m wide, nose toward the house. It almost fills the 5.50 m court depth: only 0.55 m from rear bumper to the gate line, and only 0.45 m from front bumper to the house wall. THESE TWO SMALL GAPS ARE CRITICAL. There is no extra paved apron inside the gate, no planting or staircase between the car nose and wall, and no wide passage in front of or behind the car. Draw the gate threshold immediately behind the rear bumper. Show the nose almost touching the wall under the small ground-floor bathroom window with only the narrow stated gap.
The lot frontage is 10 m, building facade 9 m, left side passage 1 m. The car enters through a 3.20 m opening at the left. One dark horizontal-slatted SLIDING gate retracts sideways into a central pocket to the right of the vehicle opening, like the model, not inward toward the car. Keep that opening visibly narrow enough for one car. Separate pedestrian entry at right. Plants and modest entrance steps are confined to the pedestrian zone to the RIGHT of the car. No deep garden in the parking lane.
Preserve the facade opening arrangement: two small high upper bathroom windows on left, one small downstairs bathroom window at left, narrow laundry window beside the near-center entry, and a full two-story open flower-pattern terracotta screen on right with two separate stair windows behind. Roof cap nearly level across facade; no extra stair tower. Adopted floor level 3.40 m, ground clear height 3.0 m, upper clear height 2.8 m, illustrative roof cap near 6.7 m.
Retain warm lived-in Las Juntas/Puerto Vallarta materials and restrained tropical planting, but show a compact practical urban front court. Neighboring boundary walls may frame the site, not enlarge the lot. No extra cars, no tall garden hiding the bumper gaps, no new windows, no balcony, no text/diagram lines/dimensions/logos/watermarks. Turn the model into a real building while preserving the measured parking fit.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit Image 1, the rear architectural view, ONLY to coordinate the visible KITCHEN INTERIOR through the ground-floor LEFT sliding doors with the updated kitchen plan in Image 2.
Preserve the rear building exterior exactly: cream stucco, one upper bedroom window on viewer LEFT, solid upper-right wall, recessed upper rear wall and lower ledge, separate lower-left sliding doors and lower-right living window, slim timber-soffit canopy, outdoor table, chairs, terrace tiles, camera, warm light and planting. Do not add or relocate exterior openings.
Inside the LEFT sliding doors, beyond the indoor dining area, the kitchen now has one straight 3.60 m counter, with the sink and cooktop on that back counter, and a single 80 cm-wide fridge against the side wall. The short sink return has been removed. The plan's right exterior wall appears on the VIEWER LEFT in this rear view: show the refrigerator toward the FAR LEFT inside the kitchen, largely in side/three-quarter view facing inward to the viewer's right. Sink is on the back countertop toward the viewer-left, with cooktop farther to the viewer-right, separated by a preparation surface. The far-right end of the visible kitchen counter toward the entry hall is LOW cabinetry, not a refrigerator.
The fridge is near the sink against the viewer-left return wall, NOT standing in the hallway and not centered as a feature on the back wall. It may be partially occluded by the sliding-door jamb or interior dining furniture, consistent with real geometry. Keep timber cabinetry, pale countertop and modest warm lighting. Make the kitchen legible without making it brighter than the exterior. The living room through the RIGHT window stays unchanged.
Image 2 is a dimensioned plan reference only; do not reproduce its text, colors, labels, symbols or diagram. Keep the original square composition, no new text, no logos, no watermarks, no extra appliances.
